title: Defensive call protocol and client retry surface v2
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Background: Multiple services and client SDKs have different semantics for retrying transient failures, hedged requests, and idempotency keys. This leads to production incidents where clients either over-retry (thundering) or lose correctness due to non-deterministic duplicate side-effects. We also observe gaps in multi-region failover where retries interact poorly with per-region circuit breakers and global load-shedding policies.

Goal: Define and implement a single defensive call protocol (HTTP-level headers + clear client semantics) and a streamlined SDK surface that all Redwood services and public SDKs adopt. The protocol should make hedged requests explicit, standardize idempotency handshake and TTL, unify timeout/backoff defaults by SLO tiers, and prescribe circuit-breaker and load-shedding interactions.

Non-goals: Does NOT change business-level at-least-once vs exactly-once guarantees for legacy services; does not attempt to fully remove server-side retry logic (some infra will remain), but specifies interaction rules.

High-level spec summary:
- Headers and handshake: Introduce X-Idempotency-Key (UUID v4 or client-provided), X-Idempotency-TTL (seconds), X-Retry-Role {primary|retry|hedge}, X-Hedged {0|1} (client intention). Server responds with Idempotency-Ack: {accepted|replayed|conflict} and Idempotency-Expires header.
- Hedged semantics: When X-Hedged=1, clients may issue k parallel requests (default k=2 for high-latency SLOs) with identical X-Idempotency-Key and X-Retry-Role set to appropriate values. Servers must ensure single side-effect application using the idempotency store and respond with 200 for first completion and a deterministic status for subsequent hedges (Idempotency-Ack: replayed).
- Retry/backoff defaults: SDKs adopt SLO-driven presets: "interactive" (latency SLO <200ms) => short timeout 250ms, max attempts 2, exponential backoff base 2x; "batch" (throughput, SLO >1s) => timeout 1200ms, attempts 4, jittered backoff. These presets are configurable per-route.
- Timeout hierarchy: client deadline <= route-level SLO config <= service circuit-breaker window. If client deadline exceeds SLO, client must trim to SLO.
- Circuit-breaker & load-shedding interplay: Services expose a header X-CB-State {closed|open|half-open} and accept a graceful-fail policy when CB open (429 + Retry-After). Load-shedding should prefer rejecting hedged requests first and preserve non-idempotent primary requests where possible.
- Observability: Standard opentracing tags and logs for idempotency-key, hedge-id, attempt-number, final-result, and cb-state. SDKs emit structured telemetry so Console can attribute cost and latencies per attempt.

Migration plan:
1) Implement server-side idempotency store adapters (redis-backed) behind a feature flag.
2) Add header parsing and Idempotency-Ack responses to runtime endpoints (canary in us-west-2).
3) Release SDK patch (Node, Python, Go) with new retry surface and presets behind opt-in flag.
4) Turn on default hedging for interactive SLO routes in non-critical tenants after 2 weeks of canary.
5) Iterate on SLO presets based on telemetry for 4 weeks, then flip opt-in default.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Idempotency store becomes hot. Mitigation: local shard partitioning + bounded TTLs + fallback to coordinated single-writer path (with 429s).
- Risk: Hedging amplifies load during partial outage. Mitigation: runtime rejects hedged requests when CB open or when system-wide shed ratio exceeded; SDK lowers default k to 1 when global shed active.

Dependencies: ENG-74123, ENG-67245 (resilience infra lifecycle), infra work to expose CB state to API gateway.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runtime accepts and responds to X-Idempotency-Key and returns Idempotency-Ack in canary.
2) SDKs implement new retry surface and default presets with feature flag.
3) Integration test harness demonstrates exactly-one side-effect for hedged requests against canary service.
4) Console receives attempt-level telemetry and shows per-request breakdown.
5) Runbook updated with hedged-failure diagnosis and rollback steps.
comments: 2025-02-13: Kickoff meeting notes - agreed to keep hedging opt-in until telemetry is stable. Action: infra to prototype idempotency store (A. Singh).
2025-02-20: Design review - security asked for TTL limits and HSM audit for idempotency keys used in billing flows. Security review required. (L. Morales)
2025-02-28: Runtime canary deployed in us-west-2 behind feature flag; basic Idempotency-Ack returned for synthetic tests. Observability tags in place.
2025-03-03: SDK patch published to alpha channels. Two integration tests failing intermittently related to race on hedged completion; engineering investigating coordinated single-writer fallback.
2025-03-05: Decided to default k=1 for hedges in SDK unless route explicitly marked hedging-friendly. Updated acceptance criteria to require deterministic replay responses.
notes: Proto-API: use X-Idempotency-Key: <uuid> and X-Idempotency-TTL seconds. Servers must persist key->result mapping for TTL+buffer. Use Idempotency-Ack: replayed|accepted|conflict. Documented in SDK migration guide.
next_steps:
1) Finish single-writer fallback implementation and add integration tests (due 2025-03-12).
2) Security review thread to close by 2025-03-10.
3) Prepare runbook and rollout playbook for canary->regional->global promotion.
notes_for_oncall: If runtime sees >1% Idempotency-Store error rate, flip feature flag off and notify reliability channel. During CB open, check shed-ratio and lower SDK hedging via remote config.
